strengths: Correctly recognizes abundant canonical astrocyte markers: GFAP, AQP4, ALDH1L1, SLC1A2, GJA1, FGFR3
Identifies DLPFC/astrocyte-enriched markers such as SLC14A1, ETNPPL, SLC39A12, SLCO1C1
Explicitly checks absence of neuronal, oligodendroglial, OPC, microglial and vascular markers
weaknesses: Stops at the generic astrocyte level and does not formalize the supported mature astrocyte refinement
Mentions neuronal-like markers but does not formally classify them as minor secondary signal

strengths: Matches the majority astrocyte branch while also offering mature astrocyte (CL:0002627) as a rank-2 candidate
Aligned with the adult DLPFC mature astrocyte markers SLC14A1, ETNPPL, SLC39A12, SLC1A2, AQP4, ALDH1L1
Supports the hierarchical refinement from astrocyte to mature astrocyte
weaknesses: Primary label is generic astrocyte; the more specific mature astrocyte candidate has lower rank/score
Limited reasoning on why mature astrocyte is preferred over the simple astrocyte label

clusterProfiler.predicted_cell_type: Radial Glial Cell / Neural Progenitor Cell
strengths: Detects shared glial/developmental markers PAX6, GLI3, GFAP, ID4
Correctly notes the absence of mature neuronal markers such as RBFOX3, SYT1, SNAP25
weaknesses: Uses shared glial/astrocyte markers to infer a non-hierarchical radial glial branch without branch-specific evidence
Lacks radial-glia-specific markers such as VIM, NES, SOX2, HES5
Ignores the strong mature astrocyte functional enrichment (glutamate transport, astrocyte projection, astrocytic glutamate-glutamine uptake)

supporting: Mature/adult astrocyte markers: SLC14A1, ETNPPL, SLC39A12, SLCO1C1, ALDH1L1, SLC1A2, AQP4, GJA1, GFAP
Enrichment evidence: astrocyte projection, glial cell projection, L-glutamate import across plasma membrane, Astrocytic Glutamate-Glutamine Uptake And Metabolism
PMID 32104705 supports astrocyte identity in this brain context
conflicting: Radial glial enrichment call is based on shared markers GFAP, PAX6, GLI3, ID4 and lacks radial-glia-specific support
Minor neuronal-like markers STON2 and GRIN2C are present but do not override the dominant astrocyte identity
